overview: CNOOC Limited is the dominant offshore crude oil and natural gas exploration and production company in China and one of the largest independent E&P companies in the world, majority-owned by state-controlled China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC Group). The company explores, develops, produces and sells crude oil and natural gas from core offshore China basins (Bohai, Western/Eastern South China Sea, East China Sea) plus onshore unconventional gas, supplemented by an overseas portfolio spanning more than 20 countries including Guyana, Brazil, the US Gulf of Mexico, UK North Sea, Nigeria, Uganda, Indonesia and Australia. As of year-end 2025 it held net proved reserves of ~7.77 billion BOE and produced a record 777.3 million BOE, roughly 69% from China and 31% overseas.

business_model.summary: Pure-play upstream oil and gas producer: revenue comes almost entirely from selling crude oil and natural gas produced from owned and partnered fields, priced off international benchmarks (Brent/Dubai/Oman/WTI for oil) and negotiated long-term contracts (for gas/LNG). Profitability is a direct function of production volumes, realized oil/gas prices, and unit lifting/all-in costs (full-cycle cost of ~US$27.90/BOE in FY2025, US$29.70/BOE in H1 2026). There is no significant downstream refining/retail business - CNOOC Limited is distinct from parent CNOOC Group's broader chemicals/trading operations.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - crude sold mainly to CNOOC Group, Sinopec Group and private refiners in China plus international/domestic buyers overseas; gas sold under long-term contracts to CNOOC Gas and Power Group, China BlueChemical, Hong Kong Castle Peak Power and coastal industrial/utility customers
business_model.geographic_mix: China ~69% of net production / ~65% of reserves (2025); Overseas ~31% of production / ~35.5% of reserves, concentrated in South America (Guyana, Brazil - now the largest overseas reserve/production region), North America, Africa (Nigeria, Uganda), Asia-Pacific (Indonesia, Australia) and Europe (UK North Sea, interest in Russia's Arctic LNG 2)

competitive_position.market_position: Largest offshore oil and gas producer in China with a government-granted near-monopoly on offshore exploration cooperation with foreign partners (CNOOC Group holds the exclusive right to enter production-sharing contracts with foreign contractors in offshore China, transferred to the Company); one of the world's larger independent E&Ps by production and reserves, though far smaller than supermajors

moat_factors.description: Exclusive statutory right (via CNOOC Group) to license foreign-partnered exploration and development of offshore China acreage, a structural barrier competitors cannot replicate
All-in cost of ~US$28-30/BOE is competitive versus global peers, aided by shallow-water Bohai assets and improving recovery technology

State-controlled parent CNOOC Group and Chinese government support provide stable low-cost funding and strategic priority access to domestic offshore blocks and overseas deals (e.g. Guyana Stabroek, Brazil pre-salt), but also creates governance and geopolitical overhang
Interests in some of the world's best new deepwater plays (Guyana's Stabroek block, Brazil's Mero/Buzios) reduce reliance on mature China fields and tap industry-leading decline curves

weaknesses: Pure commodity-price taker with no downstream integration to smooth earnings volatility
Minority, non-operating interests in several key overseas projects (e.g. 25% in Stabroek, Russia's Arctic LNG 2) limit control over pace and economics of growth
State ownership invites geopolitical/sanctions risk independent of operating performance
Heavy natural decline rates on mature China offshore fields require continuous capex just to hold production flat

growth_drivers: Reserve replacement and exploration: six-plus new discoveries per year, large shallow-lithologic finds (e.g. 100-million-ton Qinhuangdao 29-6 in Bohai) and deepwater/subsea technology breakthroughs sustaining reserve life
Production growth target of 780-800 million BOE for FY2026 (record 777.3 million BOE in FY2025, +7% YoY; H1 2026 production +3.7% YoY to a record 398.7 million BOE)

Overseas deepwater megaprojects: Guyana Stabroek block (25% interest; Yellowtail and other projects ramping, 8 projects expected onstream by 2030) and Brazil pre-salt (Mero and Buzios fields, with Buzios8 onstream in H1 2026 and 11 Buzios units expected by 2027; first-time operator role on a new Santos Basin block)
Onshore unconventional (coalbed methane) gas expansion in the Ordos/Qinshui basins, with deep coalbed methane now >80% of new reserve additions there
2026 capex budget of RMB112-122 billion funding ~80+ projects under construction, continuing the multi-year production growth program

"Second curve" new-energy build-out - offshore wind (16MW floating platform, Hainan CZ7, "Haiyou Anlan" tension-leg wind project commissioned August 2026) and CCS/CCUS (China's first offshore CCUS project, Daya Bay feasibility study) diversifying beyond oil and gas longer term
Shareholder-friendly capital return policy: payout ratio floor of no less than 45% of net profit for 2025-2027

business.risk: Natural decline of mature China offshore fields
business.description: Continuous capex and technology (fine water flooding, infill drilling) required just to hold the ~9.5% natural decline rate; failure to execute capacity projects on time could slow growth
Company discloses high concentration among both major customers (CNOOC Group, Sinopec Group) and major suppliers, creating disruption risk if either relationship deteriorates

business.risk: Limited control over joint ventures/partnered projects
business.description: Minority, non-operated stakes in key overseas growth assets (Stabroek, Arctic LNG 2) constrain CNOOC's influence over pace, cost and economics
Typhoons, marine transport hazards, oil spill/blowout risk and cyber/IT security threats could cause casualties, environmental damage and reputational harm with potential loss of operating licenses
Company flags risk that anticipated benefits of past and future acquisitions/disposals (e.g. 2025 Gulf of Mexico INEOS transaction) may not be realized

financial.description: Revenue substantially in RMB and USD; RMB depreciation helps reported oil/gas revenue but raises imported equipment costs, and overseas capex funded by converting RMB to USD creates FX risk

financial.risk: Foreign exchange control / dividend remittance risk
financial.description: Capital controls in some host countries could restrict remittance of overseas subsidiary cash flows back to the group

regulatory.risk: US sanctions / Chinese military-linked company designations
regulatory.description: CNOOC was added to the US Department of Defense's Section 1260H list of Chinese military-linked companies in December 2020 and subsequently placed on the OFAC Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies (CMIC) list (effective August 2021), barring US persons from purchasing CNOOC securities; this contributed to CNOOC's 2021 delisting from the NYSE. Escalation of US-China tensions could broaden restrictions further and depress index inclusion/foreign ownership

regulatory.risk: China oil and gas sector reform / market liberalization
regulatory.description: Loosening of China's foreign-investment restrictions on oil and gas E&P (and the new Mineral Resources Law effective July 2025) could increase competition for exploration rights that CNOOC Group previously controlled on an exclusive basis

China's carbon peak/neutrality targets and global decarbonization policy could raise compliance costs, curb fossil-fuel investment economics, and expose the company to reputational/ESG risk from investors

regulatory.risk: Geopolitical sanctions on specific overseas assets
regulatory.description: CNOOC's 10% interest in Arctic LNG 2 LLC in Russia has been adversely affected by Russia-Ukraine sanctions; other overseas assets could face similar exposure depending on host-country geopolitics

macro.description: Realized oil price fell 13.4% YoY in FY2025 (US$66.47/bbl) versus FY2024; the business is a price-taker with earnings directly levered to Brent/Dubai/WTI benchmarks, OPEC+ supply decisions, and global demand growth, particularly from China
Management specifically cited rising expectations of global liquidity tightening and macro uncertainty weighing on H1 2026 conditions, alongside sharp oil price swings
Accelerating global shift to renewables and EVs could structurally dampen long-term oil demand growth, pressuring long-cycle project economics

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global upstream oil and gas remains in a mature, cyclical phase with OPEC+ supply management and China demand growth as key swing factors; offshore and deepwater (Guyana, Brazil pre-salt) remain the industry's lowest-cost growth frontier, which benefits CNOOC's overseas portfolio
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - revenue and profit are directly tied to the oil price cycle; FY2020 (COVID oil crash) net income fell to RMB24,956m from RMB61,045m the prior year, illustrating full cyclical exposure
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct balance-sheet sensitivity (modest leverage, net cash position improving over time) but moderate indirect sensitivity via global liquidity conditions affecting oil demand and capital markets

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 results: record interim revenue of RMB242.7bn (+16.9% YoY) and record net profit of RMB85.8bn (+23.4% YoY); record H1 production of 398.7 million BOE (+3.7% YoY); declared record interim dividend of HK$0.94/share (45.2% payout, ~RMB38.8bn total)
China's first tension-leg floating wind power project, 'Haiyou Anlan', commissioned and connected to the grid; construction of the CZ7 deep-sea wind demonstration project progressing

Acquired three new overseas exploration blocks in Brazil and Indonesia; made four new China discoveries and appraised 16 oil/gas-bearing structures; first-time acquisition of an operated block in Brazil's Santos Basin pre-salt

Mixed analyst sentiment: CLSA Buy (HK$36 target, June 2026) and Citi Buy (HK$33, April 2026) versus Macquarie Sell (HK$17.80, April 2026); consensus skews Buy with average 12-month target near HK$33 against a share price around HK$22-23
Record Q1 2026 net production of 205.1 million BOE (+8.6% YoY), driven partly by Kenli 10-2 and Guyana's Yellowtail project ramp-up

FY2025 revenue RMB398.2bn (-5.4% YoY) and net profit RMB122.1bn (-11.5% YoY) on a 13.4% decline in realized oil price, partly offset by record production of 777.3 million BOE (+7% YoY); all-in cost held at US$27.90/BOE; final dividend of HK$0.55/share bringing full-year FY2025 dividend to HK$1.28/share (45% payout)
Leadership changes: Huang Yongzhang appointed Vice Chairman, CEO and President; prior Chairman Wang Dongjin and CEO Zhou Xinhuai departed; several independent non-executive directors also departed

Completed Stock Purchase Agreement with INEOS Energy for non-operating US Gulf of Mexico interests (Appomattox, Stampede fields); continued Guyana Stabroek appraisal success (Lukanani, Ranger) and Yellowtail/Buzios7 (Brazil) startups

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report / FY2025 Annual Report

items.notes: Up from the record 777.3 million BOE achieved in FY2025; reaffirmed at the H1 2026 update after record first-half output of 398.7 million BOE
Funds continued development of 80+ projects under construction, exploration, and new-energy (offshore wind/CCUS) investment

items.target: no less than 45% of net profit
items.notes: Multi-year payout floor announced in the company's 2025 strategy plan; FY2025 payout was 45% (HK$1.28/share total); H1 2026 interim payout ratio was 45.2% (HK$0.94/share, record interim dividend)

items.target: cost discipline, no explicit numeric target disclosed beyond trend
items.notes: All-in cost was US$27.90/BOE for FY2025 and US$29.70/BOE in H1 2026 (higher reflecting cost inflation/mix); management continues to emphasize cost competitiveness as a strategic priority

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Zhang Chuanjiang's H1 2026 statement emphasized record production and profit despite 'sharp fluctuations in international oil prices' and 'rising expectations of global liquidity tightening.' Management reiterated it will 'spare no effort' in H2 2026 to meet annual production targets, grow reserves, advance new-energy initiatives (offshore wind, CCUS) and maintain safety, while continuing the strategic pivot toward a dual oil/gas 'First Curve' plus new-energy 'Second Curve' growth model.

bull_case: Record and growing production (780-800 million BOE FY2026 target) from a low-cost (~US$28-30/BOE all-in) asset base gives CNOOC above-peer volume growth even in a flat-to-lower oil price environment

Exposure to the industry's best new deepwater growth plays - Guyana's Stabroek block and Brazil's pre-salt Mero/Buzios fields - provides a multi-year production growth runway largely independent of mature China basin decline
Attractive, policy-committed shareholder returns with a dividend payout floor of at least 45% of net profit through 2027, delivering a high and growing dividend yield even through the oil price cycle
State-granted structural monopoly on foreign-partnered offshore China exploration provides a durable, hard-to-replicate competitive moat domestically
Consensus analyst sentiment skews Buy, with several brokers (CLSA, Citi, First Shanghai) seeing meaningful upside to current trading levels on a cheap earnings multiple
bear_case: Pure-play commodity exposure means earnings remain highly levered to volatile oil prices - FY2025 net profit fell 11.5% on a 13.4% drop in realized oil price, and a sustained downturn (as in 2020) can cut profits by more than half

US sanctions designation (DoD 1260H list and OFAC CMIC list) caps foreign institutional ownership, contributed to the 2021 NYSE delisting, and could tighten further amid rising US-China tensions, structurally depressing the valuation multiple and liquidity versus global E&P peers

State ownership and governance ties to CNOOC Group/the Chinese government create policy, capital-allocation and geopolitical risks (e.g., sanctioned 10% Arctic LNG 2 stake in Russia) that are largely outside minority shareholders' influence
Minority, non-operated interests in several marquee growth projects (Stabroek 25%, Arctic LNG 2 10%) limit CNOOC's control over development pace, costs and ultimate economics

Secular energy transition and accelerating global decarbonization policy could compress long-term oil demand growth and the terminal value of CNOOC's reserve base, even as the company's own new-energy ('Second Curve') business remains small relative to core oil and gas
